quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #17
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: When riding in a vehicle, small children:

options.text: May be safely held by a strong adult.
Will be safe if they stand on the floor in the back of the vehicle.
Will not be hurt in an accident because they are small.
Must never be allowed to ride while standing in the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must never be allowed to ride while standing in the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Children who are too small for regular safety belts need special child seats. No adult is strong enough to hold a child safely during an accident or sudden stop. Children must always be properly fastened into a seat.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle:

options.text: In a curve or on a hill because few vehicles are coming.
By driving on the shoulder of the highway.
If your lane has a solid yellow line and the passing lane is clear.

questions.explanation: Do not pass on hills or in curves because you cannot see oncoming traffic and may crash. Never drive on the shoulder to pass. Never cross a solid yellow line to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line next to your lane means you cannot pass from your direction.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the bridge or overpass ahead has low clearance. Do not proceed if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign.

questions.question: An arrow painted on the pavement means:

options.text: Drivers in that lane may make the movement shown by the arrow if they choose.
Drivers in that lane must make the movement shown by the arrow only if traffic lights are not working.
Drivers in that lane must always stop completely before making the movement shown by the arrow.
Drivers in that lane must make the movement shown by the arrow while obeying traffic signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers in that lane must make the movement shown by the arrow while obeying traffic signals.
questions.explanation: An arrow painted on the pavement tells drivers in that lane they must make the movement shown by the arrow. Follow all traffic signs and signals before proceeding in the direction of the arrow.

questions.question: Drivers may pass on a two-lane roadway marked with a single solid yellow line on their side of the centerline.
questions.explanation: You may only pass when the broken yellow line is on your side of the centerline. A solid yellow line on your side means no passing.

questions.question: A good rule to remember for passing is:

options.text: Pass on the right whenever possible.
Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only when needed.
Move to the front of slow traffic so you can see better.
Always flash your lights and honk your horn to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only when needed.
questions.explanation: Each pass increases the chance of a crash. If you drive faster than surrounding traffic, you will need to pass constantly. Drive with traffic flow within the speed limit and only pass when necessary.

questions.question: Two solid yellow lines on the pavement mean:

options.text: Passing is allowed for drivers from both directions.
Passing is allowed if you are at the top of a hill.
Passing is allowed during daylight only.

questions.explanation: Yellow lines show that traffic on the other side is moving toward you. Never cross two solid yellow lines to pass from either direction.

questions.question: Which light tells you to slow down and proceed with caution at an intersection?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, proceed with caution, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: This sign tells you that:

options.text: No turns are allowed on this road.
The road may be slippery when wet.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead has three or more curves.

questions.question: Traffic signals sometimes show arrows to control turns from specific lanes. A green arrow means:

options.text: It is used only on one-way streets.
It means the same as a circular green light, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
You may proceed only if the green arrow appears with a circular green light.
It shows the way to an airport.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same as a circular green light, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means the same as a circular green light. However, traffic in that lane must turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: What is the speed limit on urban or town roads if no other speed limit is posted?
questions.explanation: The speed limit on urban or town roads is 30 miles per hour unless a different speed limit is posted. Follow any posted speed limit.

questions.question: A railroad crossbuck sign should be treated the same as a yield sign.
questions.explanation: A railroad crossing crossbuck sign works like a yield sign. You must yield the right-of-way to any trains and railroad equipment.

questions.question: When must drivers yield to a pedestrian?

options.text: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.
Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as the driver.
Only if the pedestrian uses a hand signal to ask you to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians in the street, even if they are crossing against a red light or being careless.

questions.question: This sign warns drivers about:

options.text: A curve in the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A curve in the road ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the road ahead curves to the right.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Speed up to increase the distance between you.
Slam on your brakes to get them to back off.
Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors several times a minute for tailgaters or fast-approaching traffic. If a car is following too closely, slow down and let it pass. Most rear-end collisions happen because vehicles follow too closely.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Grip the steering wheel tightly and slow to a stop.
Turn on hazard flashers and continue driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the steering wheel tightly and slow to a stop.
questions.explanation: Do not slam on the brakes if your tire blows out. Hold the steering wheel firmly to stay in your lane. Slow down by releasing the accelerator. Once you are moving slowly, apply the brakes lightly and pull off the road safely.

questions.question: Your power steering stops working while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the ignition.
Turn on hazard lights and brace yourself.
Steer with extra effort, slow down, and drive to a safe area to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer with extra effort, slow down, and drive to a safe area to stop.
questions.explanation: If your power steering fails, you will need to use more force to steer. Reduce your speed and pull off the road to stop in a safe area.

questions.question: When can you proceed through an intersection with a stop sign but no stop line or crosswalk?

options.text: After slowing down to check for cross traffic.
After coming to a complete stop and checking that it is safe.
After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: After coming to a complete stop and checking that it is safe.
questions.explanation: Stop before entering any intersection with a stop sign. If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection. Proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Reduce your speed when the pavement is wet.
The road ahead has a series of turns or curves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed when the pavement is wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the pavement is slippery when wet. In wet conditions, slow down, avoid sudden braking or turning, and keep more distance from the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot, what should you do?

options.text: Move forward or back so the other driver can see you.
Honk your horn to alert them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or back so the other driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Never drive in someone's blind spot. Move forward or back so the driver can see you.

questions.question: Your speed does not affect how far your vehicle travels after you brake.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the longer it takes your vehicle to stop. Always stay far behind the vehicle in front of you, especially at high speeds.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow X on a lane control signal mean?

options.text: The signal is about to turn red.
The signal is about to turn green.
You may only use this lane to turn left.
You may drive slowly in this lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may only use this lane to turn left.
questions.explanation: Lane control signals show which lanes are open or closed. A flashing yellow X means you can only use that lane to make a left turn.

questions.question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?
questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs warn you about railroad crossings. You must yield to trains and never try to drive around the crossing gates.

questions.question: What do work zone signs mean?

options.text: You must stop and back up immediately.
You should drive faster to leave the zone.

questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange and mean construction or work is happening on the road. Drive carefully in these areas.

questions.question: Large vehicles have blind spots that can extend 200 feet behind them.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles have blind spots extending up to 200 feet behind them. Do not tailgate them because the driver cannot see you.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that there is a sharp right turn in the road ahead.

questions.question: When should you return to your lane after passing another vehicle?

options.text: When you feel far enough ahead.
When the other driver signals you to return.
When you can see the other vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
When you are next to the other vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the other vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Use your right turn signal before returning to your lane. Return only when you can see the entire vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light, who must yield?
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing at any intersection without a traffic light, whether or not there is a crosswalk.

questions.question: Roads freeze quickly when they are:
questions.explanation: In cold or wet weather, shaded areas under trees or buildings freeze faster than other road sections. They also take longer to dry.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulation signs tell drivers what they must do. This sign means U-turns are not allowed here.

questions.question: You can use parking lights instead of headlights when driving at night.
questions.explanation: You must use your headlights when driving at night. Using only parking lights is against the law.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines mean you can pass another vehicle from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing is allowed from either direction. You cannot cross these lines to pass another car.

questions.question: When headlights from oncoming cars blind you at night, where should you look?

options.text: At the center of the road
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right edge of the road to reduce glare. Do not look directly at the oncoming headlights, as this can blind you.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs show?

options.text: The fastest or slowest speed you are legally allowed to drive
The speed you should drive in heavy traffic
The speed you should drive in bad conditions

questions.correctAnswerText: The fastest or slowest speed you are legally allowed to drive
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the maximum and minimum speeds allowed on the road. You must slow down when road or weather conditions require it, even if the speed limit is higher.

questions.question: A red circle with a line through it on a sign means:

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
Some drivers must yield to others.
You must drive slower than the speed limit.

questions.explanation: A red circle with a slash means the action shown below it is forbidden. These signs are white with red and black markings.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a main road from a private driveway?

options.text: Honk your horn to warn other drivers.
Stick part of your car onto the road to alert drivers.
Drive out quickly to merge with traffic.
Let pedestrians and road traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians and road traffic go first.
questions.explanation: When leaving a driveway or private road, you must yield the right-of-way to all pedestrians and traffic on the main road.

questions.question: You approach a railroad crossing with no gates or flashing lights, but there is a crossbuck sign. What should you do?

options.text: Approach with care and only cross when you are sure no train is coming.
Turn down your radio to listen for a train.
Only go when a flagger tells you it is safe.

questions.explanation: Always approach railroad crossings with extreme caution. Only cross when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. If a flagger is present, follow their directions.

questions.question: Which statement is correct?

options.text: Signal at least 100 feet before passing and check for oncoming traffic.
Check your mirrors and look over your left shoulder for blind spots when passing left.
See both headlights of the passed car in your mirror before moving back to your lane.

questions.explanation: When passing, signal at least 100 feet ahead. Always check your mirrors and look over your shoulder. Return to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed car in your mirror.

questions.question: If you cannot safely merge into traffic, you must also stop when yielding the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: When you must yield the right-of-way, you must also stop if you cannot safely merge into the traffic flow.
